title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant

Based in Manchester
Paying up to 30k DOE
5 days on site, Monday - Friday

Working closely with the wider finance team, you'll play an important role in ensuring accurate financial information is produced on time, while also supporting the business with analysis and reporting.

We're looking for someone who can:
- Manage and prioritise competing deadlines effectively
- Analyse financial information and identify key points or discrepancies
- Work confidently with Excel and large datasets
- Take ownership of tasks and look for ways to improve processes
- Work independently while also being a strong team player
- Communicate financial information clearly and accurately

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
About the Role

We're looking for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join our team and play an important role in delivering an accurate, efficient and high-quality payroll service.

This is a hands-on role for someone who already has a good understanding of payroll and has experience managing the full end-to-end payroll process. You'll be responsible for processing payroll accurately and on time, responding to queries, investigating discrepancies and ensuring everything is completed in line with current payroll legislation and company requirements.

You don't need to know every payroll system - experience of InPay would be an advantage, but it's not essential. We're more interested in someone with strong practical payroll experience, good attention to detail and a solid understanding of UK payroll legislation.

A CIPP qualification would also be advantageous, but is not essential for the right candidate.

What You'll Be Doing
- Process full end-to-end payroll, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time.
- Process payroll data, checking information carefully and completing relevant validations.
- Respond to payroll queries received through ticketing systems and telephone, ensuring they are dealt with promptly and accurately.
- Investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies and queries.
- Process advance payments, adjustments and other payroll amendments.
- Ensure payroll is processed in line with current UK payroll legislation and statutory requirements.
- Maintain a good working knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance, tax codes, pensions and statutory payments.
- Keep up to date with relevant changes to payroll legislation.
- Handle confidential employee and financial information appropriately and in line with GDPR requirements.
- Work towards individual and team KPIs and agreed service levels.
- Complete weekly tasks and activities assigned by the Team Leader/Manager.
- Work collaboratively with other payroll teams across the department, supporting cross-training and business requirements.
- Contribute to continuous improvement, helping to identify ways to improve processes and the customer experience.
- Provide support to colleagues across the wider payroll team where required.
- Maintain accurate payroll and financial records.
- Support internal and external implementations and changes when required.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone with solid practical payroll experience who is comfortable working across the full payroll cycle.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience of full end-to-end payroll processing - essential.
- A good working knowledge of UK payroll legislation - essential.
- Experience investigating and resolving payroll queries and discrepancies.
- Experience working to deadlines, SLAs and KPIs.
- Good understanding of PAYE, National Insurance, pensions, tax codes and statutory payments.
- Previous customer service or payroll support experience.
- Good IT and systems skills, with the ability to learn new payroll systems quickly.
- CIPP qualification - desirable, but not essential.
- InPay experience - desirable, but not essential.

The Person

You'll be someone who:
- Pays attention to detail and understands the importance of getting payroll right.
- Has a good practical understanding of payroll legislation.
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities.
- Can work accurately and efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
- Is comfortable working to deadlines where accuracy is important.
- Has good communication and listening skills.
- Is confident dealing with payroll queries and providing clear and helpful responses.
- Takes ownership of issues and follows them through to resolution.
- Works well as part of a team but is also comfortable working independently.
- Understands the importance of confidentiality when dealing with personal and financial information.
- Has a positive, customer-focused approach.
- Is keen to learn and develop their payroll knowledge.

What You'll Bring

We're not looking for someone who necessarily knows every payroll system or has years of specialist payroll experience.

We're looking for someone who knows payroll, has experience managing it from start to finish and understands the legislation that sits behind it.

If you've got strong practical payroll experience, excellent attention to detail and the right attitude, we'd love to hear from you.

InPay experience and a CIPP qualification would be a bonus, but they're not a deal-breaker.

title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
Greys Specialist Recruitment are working with an established business to recruit a Supply Chain & Procurement Co-Ordinator to join its purchasing team at its site in Carrington, Trafford.

Reporting to the Group Purchasing Manager, this is a varied role combining purchasing, supplier management and day-to-day supply chain coordination. You will play an important part in ensuring materials and services are available when needed, deliveries arrive on time and stock levels are maintained to support business operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous purchasing or supply chain experience who enjoys working with suppliers, solving problems and keeping processes running efficiently within a manufacturing or similar environment.

The Role

Working closely with the Purchasing Manager and teams across the business, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating the purchasing of raw materials, consumables and services to meet operational and production requirements.
- Obtaining supplier quotations, reviewing pricing and delivery timescales, and supporting negotiations to secure competitive terms.
- Building and maintaining effective relationships with suppliers, monitoring service levels and helping to resolve delivery, quality and pricing issues.
- Monitoring stock levels and material availability to support production schedules and minimise shortages or excess inventory.
- Liaising with suppliers, logistics partners, warehouse and production teams to coordinate deliveries and resolve stock discrepancies.
- Supporting demand planning and forecasting to ensure purchasing activity aligns with business requirements.
- Maintaining accurate purchasing, supplier and stock records using internal systems and Microsoft Excel.
- Preparing reports on purchasing activity, stock levels and supplier performance, highlighting potential issues and opportunities for improvement.
- Supporting supplier approval processes and maintaining documentation in line with company procedures and ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 requirements.
- Contributing to cost-saving initiatives, waste reduction and continuous improvement projects.
- Assisting with ERP/MRP system improvements and ensuring purchasing processes remain accurate and efficient.
- Supporting internal and external audits, attending meetings and undertaking occasional UK or international supplier visits where required.

About You

We are looking for an organised and commercially minded individual with previous experience in purchasing, procurement or supply chain coordination, ideally within a manufacturing, engineering or similar operational environment.

You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, communicating with suppliers and internal departments, and taking a proactive approach to resolving issues.

You should also have:
- Experience in purchasing, supplier coordination or supply chain operations.
- A good understanding of procurement processes, stock control and delivery coordination.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, with the ability to maintain and interpret data accurately.
- Experience using an ERP, MRP or purchasing system.
- Good communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to organise your workload effectively.
- A practical approach to continuous improvement and cost efficiency.

Knowledge of Incoterms and experience supporting ISO compliance or supplier audits would be advantageous. A relevant qualification, such as CIPS or a degree in procurement or supply chain management, would also be beneficial but is not essential.

The Opportunity

This is a great opportunity to join an established business in a varied purchasing and supply chain role, working closely with an experienced Group Purchasing Manager and contributing to the smooth running of day-to-day operations.

The position offers a salary of £29,500 per annum + Bonus, a permanent contract and a Monday-to-Friday working pattern, with an earlier finish on Fridays.

Contact David at Greys Specialist Recruitment

Ensure adherence to safer recruitment practices throughout the recruitment process.

Support the tracking and analysis of recruitment data, to assist with the production of reports.

Assist with general office functions.

- Contribute to the monitoring and reporting of all safeguarding concern processes, within your teams, ensuring all concerns are reported promptly to the Designated Safeguarding Lead or deputies, and helping to promote and foster a culture of vigilance and accountability across The Tutor Trust.Take responsibility for monitoring safeguarding processes within your teams.

Collaborate with colleagues across teams and regions to ensure consistent messaging and effective communication.

Assist other staff to complete a variety of tasks that enable the Trust to operate effectively and efficiently.

Any other duties commensurate with the grade and nature of the post.

Person Specification

Strong candidates for this role will demonstrate a solid track record of performance, possess excellent IT and English skills, exhibit strong interpersonal and diplomatic abilities, and show initiative in their approach.

Skills

Communication & Interpersonal Skills

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to build rapport with stakeholders at all levels and across sectors.

Confident in representing the organisation in meetings, presentations, and events.

Organisational & Time Management

Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines effectively.

Ability to work under pressure while maintaining consistently high standards of work.

Administrative and IT Skills

Proven administrative experience in a previous paid or voluntary role.

Fully IT literate, with particular competence in Microsoft Excel and Access.

Ability to manage office systems, databases, and documentation accurately and efficiently.

Independent and Team Working Skills

Able to work collaboratively as part of a team and independently when required.

Quick to grasp new concepts and adapt to changing priorities.

Attributes

Committed to safeguarding children and young people, and willing to undergo DBS clearance.

Alignment with the goals, ethos, and mission of the Tutor Trust.

Empathy for disadvantaged and vulnerable learners.

Enthusiastic and proactive in contributing to organisational growth and success.

Excellent time-management and attention to detail.

Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative working style.

Willingness to work outside standard hours when required.

General

How to apply

To apply, download an application form, an equality and diversity monitoring form and send your completed documents to the email address provided.

The role is based on a fixed-term basis from 4th January to 30th June 2027. Your regular place of work will be the Tutor Trust Head Office in Manchester; however, the position will also involve occasional travel to our partners.

The hours of work are 36.25 hours per week over 52 weeks (hybrid working currently in operation). Holiday entitlement will be 33 days per annum (inclusive of Bank Holidays). There may also involve working occasional unsocial hours in evenings.

The Tutor Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people in line with Keeping Children Safe in Education. We expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. The Tutor Trust is an Equal Opportunities Employer. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are committed to fair treatment throughout the recruitment process and beyond.

We believe that a diverse team drives innovation and strengthens the programmes we deliver to pupils. Diversity spans many dimensions of identity, and we are committed to cultivating an inclusive, equitable workplace where every voice is heard, respected, and valued.

A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check As part of our commitment to safeguarding patients and staff, many roles at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) require a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. This is a standard process across the NHS and helps us ensure a safe environment for everyone. What is a DBS Check? A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. The level of check required depends on the role: Standard DBS : Checks for spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings. Enhanced DBS : Includes the above, plus any additional information held by local police thats considered relevant to the role. Enhanced with Barred Lists: Includes all of the above, plus checks against the childrens and/or adults barred lists. Who Needs a DBS Check Most roles involving direct patient contact, working with children or vulnerable adults, or access to sensitive information will require a DBS check. The job advert and recruitment team will let you know if this applies to your role. The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. For more information about the cost of the various types of DBS, please visit: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dbs-fees-are-changing-in-december DBS Update Service Candidates are also expected to register with the DBS Update Service which must be completed within 30 days of the certificate being issued. This helps streamline future employment checks and supports safer recruitment practices. For more information, please visit the DBS Update Service.
